updates.summary: React 19 lets function components take `ref` as a normal prop; `forwardRef` is deprecated.
changes: TL;DR — 'Use `forwardRef` to let parent components access a child's DOM node' → accept `ref` as a prop (React 19); `forwardRef` only needed before 19.

Key Concepts — `FancyInput` rewritten from `forwardRef(...)` to `function FancyInput({ label, ref, ...props })`, with a 'Before React 19' note (forwardRef still works but is deprecated); removed the `displayName` workaround.
Why It Matters / Interview Q&A — 'What is forwardRef and why is it needed?' → how `ref` reaches a child in React 19 vs the pre-19 `forwardRef` wrapper.
Coding Challenge — `ScrollableList` rewritten to take `ref` as a prop (Challenge/Solution headings unchanged).

updates.summary: With React 19's `ref` prop, `useImperativeHandle` examples no longer need `forwardRef`.
changes: TL;DR / Key Concepts — 'Used with `forwardRef`' → the `ref` arrives as a normal prop in React 19 (forwardRef import removed, pre-19 noted).
Key Concepts — `Input`, `ControlledInput` and `Modal` examples rewritten from `forwardRef(...)` to plain components with a `ref` prop.
Why It Matters / Interview Q&A — wording changed from 'forwardRef receives the ref' to 'the component receives the ref prop (React 19; forwardRef before 19)'.
Common Pitfalls — stale-deps example `ListHandle` rewritten without `forwardRef`.
Coding Challenge — `VideoPlayer` rewritten with a `ref` prop instead of `forwardRef`.

updates.summary: The Day 5 mental-model summary still said refs need `forwardRef`.
changes: Mental Model (DOM ACCESS) — 'forwardRef: lets parent access child's internal DOM node' → React 19 `ref` is a normal prop (pre-19: forwardRef).
Mental Model (useImperativeHandle) — 'Always used with forwardRef' → takes the `ref` prop (React 19) / forwardRef's ref (pre-19).

updates.summary: TanStack Query v5 has no `loading` status; `status` is pending | error | success and `isLoading` is derived.
changes: TL;DR — state machine `pending → loading → success | error` → `status` is `'pending' | 'error' | 'success'`; `isLoading` = `isPending && isFetching`.

updates.summary: Query keys are hashed deterministically (object key order ignored), not compared via plain `JSON.stringify`.
changes: Key Concepts — code comment 'TanStack Query serializes keys with JSON.stringify' → keys are hashed deterministically, object key order ignored.

updates.summary: Query keys are hashed deterministically (sorted object keys), consistent with lesson 08/03.
changes: TL;DR — 'serializes it with `JSON.stringify`' → hashes it deterministically (a JSON.stringify that sorts object keys, so property order doesn't matter).

updates.summary: Key change detection compares deterministic hashes, not plain `JSON.stringify` strings.
changes: Interview Q&A — 'serializes the current key with `JSON.stringify` and compares' → hashes the key deterministically (object keys sorted) and compares the hashes.

updates.summary: The lifecycle lists five phases, not four.
changes: TL;DR — 'four phases' → 'five phases' (fetching → fresh → stale → inactive → deleted).

updates.summary: Immer only drafts Map/Set after you call `enableMapSet()` once; otherwise it throws.
changes: TL;DR / Key Concepts — 'work fine with Immer' / 'Immer handles Set natively' → needs a one-time `enableMapSet()` at app startup (added the import and the error Immer throws without it).
Why It Matters / Interview Q&A — Immer 'natively' handles Map/Set → only after `enableMapSet()`; Zustand's `immer` middleware does not enable it.
Coding Challenge — `useMultiSelectStore` solution now calls `enableMapSet()` first.

updates.summary: The summary said Map/Set work natively with Immer; they need `enableMapSet()`.
changes: Mental Model — 'In-memory + Immer: Set/Map work natively' → 'work after a one-time enableMapSet()'.
